Compete for biodiversity achievements and outmaneuver your opponents by activating the special abilities of your plants and animals. Each action can only be activated once, so think carefully about which actions you take and when. Rounds of the game move through the seasons, each season having its own thematic impact on the Biome. In the simultaneous gameplay phase, draw cards and collect resources to play a plant or animal into your Biome and earn points. Play your birds and rabbits next to plants, so that in Spring, they will make nests and have chicks and baby bunnies! But beware, in Summer, your opponents' predators are on the prowl. Protect your baby animals by playing more plants in each habitat. Earn points with successful hunts and by feeding your baby animals. The optional Natural Disasters mini expansion (spinner) brings additional variability and nature's harsh reality to your game of Biome. This mini expansion is not yet available on Board Game Arena. With many ways to earn points (and win!) plus multiple difficulty levels, you can tailor your game to your adventure level! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Biome 1.1 Gameplay 1.2 Bonuses & Achievements 1.3 End of Game Biome In this strategic tableau-building game for 1-4 players, players act as environmentalists. The goal is to establish a flourishing, biodiverse Biome by playing flora and fauna cards, raising baby animals, and completing achievements to earn the most victory points. Gameplay The game spans a maximum of 3 years, each divided into 4 seasons. Each season consists of six phases, played either simultaneously or in turn-based order. 1. Hand Limit Check (Simultaneous): The hand limit is 8 cards. Excess cards must be discarded. For every 2 cards discarded, you receive 1 resource or 1 new card. 2. Draw Cards (Simultaneous): All players draw 2 cards from the main deck. 3. Collect Resources (Simultaneous): All players take 2 resources of their choice (Sunlight for plants, various food types for animals) from the supply. 4. Play 1 Card (Simultaneous): You may play 1 card into your Biome by paying its resource cost and advancing your token on the point track. If you decline to play a card, you may draw 1 card instead. 5. Seasonal Event (Turn-based): This phase changes with the season: Spring (Nesting): Birds and rabbits adjacent to compatible plants form nests and produce babies (chicks/kits). Summer (Predation & Feeding): Predators can attack opponents' nests (die roll). Afterward, you must pay food to feed your own baby animals to raise them for points. 6. Action Phase (Turn-based): On your turn, you may activate the ability of one unused card in your Biome. Place a player cube on the card to mark it as used. Each card ability can only be activated once per game. Bonuses & Achievements Point Track: Reaching or passing specific spaces grants instant bonuses (resources, card draws, or discounts). Achievements: The first player to complete a public achievement earns the highest point value. Subsequent players earn fewer points for the same goal. End of Game The game ends at the conclusion of a season if any of these conditions are met: A player reaches 120 points. A player's Biome (all 18 spaces) is completely filled with cards. The end of the 3rd year (12 seasons) is reached. The player with the most victory points on the track wins. [Rating: 2/10] Stupid euro with stupid luck actions, high card luck. Way worse than Eath, Wingspan or other similar Games.

[Rating: 3/10] Just not my cup of tea. I like the concept, but the execution doesn’t do it for me. Too much potential for RNG swings and as for a spinner - took me back to the classic “Nuclear War”. If you live with this then fine, but I’m moving on. Slightly disappointed as there are some nice concepts in the design.

[Rating: 3/10] Biome comes across like a remix of Wingspan and Earth with a few other elements thrown in. It looks quite nice, but the main issue I had with it is that it is longer than either of those two games, yet introduces a lot more randomness in the proceedings. While it may be somewhat faithful to its subject matter in that respect it just doesn't create an engaging game.

[Rating: 3/10] A very disappointing luck fest. Opponent completed all objectives, I couldn't do one. They had predators in all biomes, I drew none to play. Die rolls, coin flips, didn't even try the spinner module... terribly miserable game to play when it doesn't go your way, feels entirely out of your control.

[Rating: 3/10] Was very interested in this game. Unfortunately its far away from my expectation. Random points, coin toss and unneeded dice for more randomness!

[Rating: 4/10] Das Spiel wirkt für mich etwas undurchdacht und nicht so befriedigend wie Erde/Flügelschlag/...

[Rating: 4/10] Meh... definition of "just because you could make another Wingspan/Earth clone, doesn't mean you should". The random card draws can really screw someone over, especially if everyone is fulfilling the same shared goals, the nests are ugly and get in the way and the overall feel is "please make it end".

[Rating: 5/10] A card based tableau building game where players gain resources, draw more cards to build, and feed new offspring in order to gain the most points.
